topic_brief.title: Organic vs conventional farming crop yield gap
topic_brief.research_question: How much lower is crop yield under organic farming compared to conventional farming?
topic_brief.intervention_description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
important_moderators: Crop type (cereal, legume, fruit, vegetable, oilseed, root/tuber)
Crop species (wheat, maize, rice, soybean, tomato, potato, etc.)
Experiment type (long-term trial, on-farm comparison, field trial)
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

rows.title: Competitive yields in organic and agroforestry cacao cropping systems: results from 15 years of a long-term systems comparison trial in Bolivia
rows.treatment_description: MON-ORG: Organic monoculture (compost fertilization, perennial cover crop, no synthetic inputs)
rows.control_description: MON-CON: Conventional monoculture (mineral fertilizer, herbicides allowed)
rows.notes: Mean values estimated from Figure 2a bar chart. Text confirms 18% less cacao in MON-ORG vs MON-CON. SE estimated from error bars. System effect p<0.001, F=51.27. Mixture of 12 cacao varieties, 1/3 re-grafted in 2018.

rows.title: Competitive yields in organic and agroforestry cacao cropping systems: results from 15 years of a long-term systems comparison trial in Bolivia
rows.treatment_description: AFS-SUC: Successional agroforestry (organic management, no external inputs, high diversity, dynamic agroforestry principles)
rows.control_description: AFS-CON: Conventional agroforestry (market-oriented, mineral fertilizer at 50% of monoculture rate)
rows.notes: AFS-SUC value estimated from Figure 2a. AFS-CON = 527 from text. CAUTION: This comparison confounds organic vs conventional management WITH system design differences (successional vs market-oriented). AFS-SUC has much higher shade tree density and crop diversity. AFS-SUC had lowest cacao yields, marked 'D' in Fig 2a. MON-CON was 2.4 times higher than AFS-SUC.

moderators.mod_planting_density: 625 cacao trees/ha + high density associated species

rows.title: Meteorological fluctuations define long-term crop yield patterns in conventional and organic production systems
rows.outcome: Corn grain yield (least squared mean, ANCOVA-adjusted for precipitation and heat stress)
rows.treatment_description: Organic corn (3 rotations pooled: 2-yr corn-soybean, 3-yr corn-soybean-wheat, 6-yr corn-soybean-wheat-alfalfa-alfalfa-alfalfa; legume cover crops, alfalfa, poultry litter for N; USDA NOP standards)
rows.control_description: Conventional corn (2 systems pooled: no-tillage and chisel-tillage; herbicide and fertilizer programs, genetically modified cultivars)
rows.notes: Least squared means from ANCOVA adjusting for precipitation and heat stress covariates, not raw means. n values are total plot-year observations across all systems and years within each management group. Paper reports 31% yield reduction. When weed cover added as additional covariate, gap reduced from 31% to 16%. 1999 data excluded (extreme drought killed crops); 2003 conventional corn excluded (wet weather prevented standard management).

moderators.mod_soil_type: silt loam (Christiana, Matapeake, Keyport, Mattapex series)
moderators.mod_analysis: ANCOVA with precipitation and heat stress as covariates

rows.title: Meteorological fluctuations define long-term crop yield patterns in conventional and organic production systems
rows.outcome: Soybean grain yield (least squared mean, ANCOVA-adjusted for precipitation and heat stress)
rows.treatment_description: Organic soybean (3 rotations pooled: 2-yr corn-soybean, 3-yr corn-soybean-wheat, 6-yr corn-soybean-wheat-alfalfa-alfalfa-alfalfa; legume cover crops, alfalfa, poultry litter for N; USDA NOP standards)
rows.control_description: Conventional soybean (2 systems pooled: no-tillage and chisel-tillage; herbicide and fertilizer programs, genetically modified cultivars)
rows.notes: Least squared means from ANCOVA adjusting for precipitation and heat stress covariates, not raw means. n values are total plot-year observations across all systems and years within each management group. Paper reports 20% yield reduction. When weed cover added as additional covariate, gap reduced from 20% to 7%. 2010 organic soybean excluded (seed shattered before harvest). Conventional soybean n differs slightly between correlation (134) and regression (131) analyses in Table 1; using 134. P-value for organic vs conventional soybean comparison not explicitly stated in text (only corn stated as P<0.05).

rows.title: Lessons From 20 Years of Studies of Wheat Genotypes in Multiple Environments and Under Contrasting Production Systems
rows.outcome: Grain yield (network-wide mean across all sites and years)
rows.treatment_description: Organic management (OM): ~90 kg N ha-1 as liquid manure, no synthetic pesticides or mineral fertilizers, 380 seeds m-2, 11 sites, 1998-2018, 102 genotypes total
rows.control_description: Conventional low-inputs (LM): 150 kg N ha-1, no fungicide, 350 seeds m-2, ~10 sites, 1998-2018, 300 genotypes total
rows.notes: CAUTION: Organic and conv-low networks were at different sites with different genotypes. The 33.5% gap overstates the true system effect. With common genotypes in last 3 overlapping years, HM-OM=20.23 and HM-LM=14.32 dt/ha, so LM-OM=5.91 dt/ha (~8.4% gap). Overall means: OM=46.86 from 11 organic sites, LM=70.40 from ~10 LM sites. 3 replications per plot at each site. Units: 1 dt/ha = 100 kg/ha.

moderators.mod_note: Networks conducted at DIFFERENT sites with DIFFERENT genotypes and partially overlapping time periods; yield difference of 23.54 dt/ha includes site and genotype confounding. With common genotypes in last 3 years, OM-LM gap narrows to ~5.91 dt/ha (p<0.05), suggesting most of the 33% gap is confounded.
